analysis:
This PR changes only test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/. EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift has modified assertions around lines 713-755. Those assertions pin the Gemma 4 wide plain prefill chunk (prefillChunkSize == widePrefillChunkTokens, soloPrefillStripeTokens == nil) and check that the paged pool's maxPrefillChunk stays sized from max(chunk, stripe). The new widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry test checks that the wide-chunk opt-in does not resize the pool. EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift is a new file; only its metadata and patch header were visible, so I could not read its body.

The tests add no production code and no new attack surface. They use hermetic environments (crash-guard path /dev/null, a temp-dir SSD root, an ephemeral KEK, SymmetricKey(size: .bits256)) and contain no real secrets. They do not weaken any mitigation in T-041. The SSD cache tests continue to assert that legacy construction is refused and that the kill switches (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, the paged kill switch) are honored.

The tests encode a security-relevant invariant: the paged pool must be sized to match the engine's scheduled prefill chunk. A mismatch would hit a PagedSequenceKV precondition, a process kill, which is a DoS on the provider (T-010/T-029 class). The tests guard against that regression.

Remaining question for integration: the production changes behind these tests (EngineV2Factory wide-chunk geometry, prefill chunk and step token budget env overrides) are outside this batch. Whether they preserve pool sizing, memory bounds and the per-request KV budget cannot be verified from tests alone. No finding is warranted on the supplied evidence.
